title: Reactive Approach vs. Prophylactic Intervention for Diffuse Bleeding in Post-Cardiopulmonary Bypass Coagulopathy
summary:
This study looks at whether giving blood-clotting medication early and generously (“Hit Hard and Early”) during planned heart valve surgeries leads to better outcomes than a more cautious, wait-and-see approach (“Watch and Wait”). We examine both the medical results and the cost implications.

We included adult patients undergoing elective, minimally invasive aortic valve replacement. Patients were excluded if they hadn’t paused certain blood-thinning medications in time before surgery, or if they had inherited clotting disorders, low platelet counts, or end-stage kidney disease.

Patients who received ROTEM—a blood clotting test—during surgery or shortly after, and were treated based on its results before any visible bleeding occurred, were placed in the “Hit Hard and Early” group. Those who received ROTEM only after signs of bleeding, or not at all, were assigned to the “Watch and Wait” group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients who have undergone elective minimally invasive aortic valve replacement between 1 Jul 2022 and 31 Oct 2025 are included.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who did not discontinue preoperative medication affecting blood coagulation in a timely manner (DOAC > 48 hours, ADP receptor antagonists 5 days) are excluded. Patients with congenital coagulation disorders, thrombocytopenia, and end-stage renal failure are also excluded.
